title: Which number has one two, two threes and one eleven as primes?
description: A number is described only by its primes: one two, two threes and one eleven. The primes are written as a row and multiplied in small groups to find the number.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number is the multiplication of the primes in its prime factorisation. Watch for students who add the primes or leave out a repeated prime.

video_script.why: The child finds a number from its primes by multiplying them in small groups, the way the book multiplies the primes of seventy two.
video_script.substitution: the book's own primes: one two, two threes and one eleven
video_script.anchor: a row of four prime tiles, one two, two threes and one eleven
video_script.payoff_line: Multiplying the primes of the row gives one hundred and ninety eight
maths_rules: check: the row has one 2, two 3s and one 11, and each of 2, 3 and 11 is prime
video_script.design: Four prime tiles stand in a row. The tiles are multiplied in two groups, and then the two results.

marks.book: the title card From your book appears

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a number made of primes.
<bookmark mark='tiles'/>Its prime factorisation has one two, two threes and one eleven.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which number has these primes in its prime factorisation?

beats.on_screen: the tiles stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the four prime tiles in a row with multiply signs between them

marks.way: multiply signs appear between the tiles
marks.tiles: each tile glows once, as one prime of the row

beats.colours: 2 in teal, 3s in amber, 11 in gold
narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='tiles'/>Each prime is one tile, and the row of tiles is the prime factorisation of the number.

beats.on_screen: Given: the primes are one 2, two 3s and one 11

marks.given: the primes are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the prime factorisation has one two, two threes and one eleven.
<bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the number that has these primes.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: write the primes as a row: 2 × 3 × 3 × 11

marks.row: the four tiles slide into the row 2 × 3 × 3 × 11

beats.colours: 2 in teal, 3s in amber, 11 in gold
narration: <bookmark mark='row'/>Step one, write the primes as a row. One two, two threes and one eleven give two times three times three times eleven.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: multiply in small groups: 3 × 3 = 9 and 2 × 11 = 22
narration: <bookmark mark='threes'/>Step two, multiply in small groups. Three times three is nine.
<bookmark mark='other'/>Two times eleven is twenty two.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: multiply the two results: 9 and 22 joined by a multiply sign

marks.join: the 9 and the 22 slide together with a multiply sign between them

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step three, multiply the nine and the twenty two that we found in the groups.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check the row against the question: one 2, two 3s and one 11, and each of 2, 3 and 11 is prime

marks.count: the row is lined up with the question, and each prime gets a tick

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step four, check the row against the question. It has one two, two threes and one eleven, and every one of them is a prime.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Multiplying the primes of the row gives one hundred and ninety eight. Nine times twenty two is one hundred and ninety eight.
